name: portfolio_proof_gap
description: Follow-up highlighting that employers increasingly ask "show me your work" — and LIT students have 30–70 real brand projects to show, while traditional graduates have only exams. Offer a joint webinar on "Portfolio vs. Transcript: What Employers Actually Hire For."

name: mentor_network_access
description: Emphasize the 500+ industry partnerships and practitioner mentors (Google, Zerodha, Shopify alumni). Offer to connect the school's career services team with LIT mentors for a guest session or hiring pipeline.

name: co_branded_challenge
description: Propose a pilot where the school's students tackle a real brand challenge under LIT mentorship, with the school's brand on the outcome. Positions the school as innovative and gives LIT proof-of-concept data.

name: placement_roi_case
description: Share anonymized case studies or testimonials of students who landed roles/gigs via LIT's model. Frame it as "How challenge-based learning closes the employability gap faster than add-on certifications."

name: life_skills_differentiation
description: Highlight the six-dimension model (curriculum + gigs + pulse classes + life skills + fitness + case studies) as holistic development. Offer a workshop for the school's students on one life skill (e.g., personal finance, basic home repair) as a taste of LIT's approach.

name: ai_age_relevance
description: Reference the Varun Mayya session insight: "AI tool mastery and adaptability will separate winners." Position LIT as training students to *use* AI in live campaigns, not compete with it. Offer a short talk on "Marketing in the AI Age: Why Execution Beats Memorization."

name: alternative_credential_trend
description: Send a trend piece on the rise of skills-based hiring and portfolio credentials (cite LinkedIn, Google Career Certificates, etc.). Frame LIT as the institution-level answer: "What if your students graduated with both a degree AND a portfolio that proves they can ship?"
